#!/usr/bin/env node
import { greeting } from '../src/greet.js';

const name = process.argv.slice(2).find((a) => !a.startsWith('--'));
if (!name) {
  process.stderr.write('usage: greet <name>\n');
  process.exit(2);
}
process.stdout.write(`${greeting(name)}\n`);
{
  "name": "greet-cli",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Greets people",
  "type": "module",
  "main": "index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "node --test"

}

result.builder:
Criteria the build must meet (from the issue, word for word):
- node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case
- without --shout the output is unchanged
- docs/index.md documents --shout
- after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout

Steps:
1. Read bin/greet.js, src/greet.js, test/greet.test.js, docs/index.md, README.md and .github/workflows/pages.yml. The CLI currently takes the first argument that does not start with `--` as the name and prints `Hello, <name>!` followed by a newline. The pages workflow publishes the `docs/` directory to https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ on every push to main.
2. In bin/greet.js, detect a `--shout` argument (it may come before or after the name). When present, print the same greeting converted to upper case (e.g. `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!` and a newline). Keep the name lookup so `--shout` is never taken as the name. When `--shout` is absent, the output must be byte-for-byte what it is today (`Hello, Ada!\n` for `Ada`), and the usage error with exit code 2 for a missing name must stay as it is.
3. Add tests to test/greet.test.js covering: `--shout Ada` gives `HELLO, ADA!\n`; `Ada --shout` gives the same; plain `Ada` still gives `Hello, Ada!\n`. Keep the existing tests unchanged.
4. Update docs/index.md to document the `--shout` flag: show the usage `node bin/greet.js --shout <name>` and say that it prints the greeting in upper case (e.g. `HELLO, <NAME>!`). Keep the existing content about the plain form. Because the pages workflow publishes `docs/` as-is, this change to docs/index.md is what makes the published page list `--shout` once the PR is merged to main and the workflow runs; do not change the workflow.
5. Run `npm test` and confirm every test passes. Also run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js Ada` by hand and check the outputs.
6. Open one pull request with these changes. In the PR description, state plainly that the last criterion (the published docs page listing --shout) can only be confirmed after merge, once the pages workflow has deployed; do not claim it as met before then.
result.verifier:
Work at the PR head. Run `npm test` once first and note the result for reference.

Check 1 — expect: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"
Run from the repository root: `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and also `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`, capturing stdout and the exit code.
PASS: each command exits 0 and its stdout is the greeting in upper case, i.e. `HELLO, ADA!` followed by a newline.
FAIL: either command exits non-zero, prints a mixed- or lower-case greeting, treats `--shout` as the name, or prints anything other than the upper-case greeting.

Check 2 — expect: "without --shout the output is unchanged"
Run `node bin/greet.js Ada` and `node bin/greet.js Grace` at the PR head. Then check out the PR's base commit (the merge base) in a separate temporary worktree and run the same two commands there. Also run `node bin/greet.js` with no arguments in both and compare stderr and exit code.
PASS: for every command, stdout, stderr and exit code at the PR head are identical to those at the base (e.g. `Hello, Ada!\n`, and for no arguments `usage: greet <name>` on stderr with exit code 2).
FAIL: any difference in stdout, stderr or exit code between the PR head and the base for a command without `--shout`.

Check 3 — expect: "docs/index.md documents --shout"
Run `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` at the PR head and read the matching section of the file.
PASS: docs/index.md exists at the PR head and contains the `--shout` flag with a description of what it does (upper-case greeting).
FAIL: docs/index.md has no `--shout`, or mentions it without saying what it does.

Check 4 — expect: "after merge, the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ lists --shout"
This can only be decided after the PR is merged and the pages workflow (.github/workflows/pages.yml, which publishes `docs/` on push to main) has deployed. Find out whether the PR is merged (e.g. `gh pr view <number> --json state,mergedAt`) and, if so, whether the pages workflow run for the merge commit has completed (`gh run list --workflow pages.yml`). Then fetch the live page: `curl -sSL https://o.github.io/greet-cli/` and search the response for `--shout`.
PASS: the PR is merged, the pages deploy for the merge commit has completed successfully, and the fetched page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ contains `--shout`.
FAIL: the PR is not merged yet, the deploy has not completed or failed, the page cannot be fetched, or the fetched page does not contain `--shout`. Do not pass this check on the strength of the diff or of docs/index.md at the PR head; if it is not yet merged, report FAIL and say the check is pending merge and deployment.

Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL condition):
- Note whether test/greet.test.js gained tests for `--shout` and whether `npm test` passes.
- Try `node bin/greet.js --shout` with no name and note whether it still prints the usage error with exit code 2.

text:
The harness accepted both briefs for issue #12 (`--shout` flag). I made no changes to the repo.

One of the four expect lines can't pass on the pull request alone. The fourth says the published docs page at https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ must list `--shout`. That can only be checked after the merge, once `.github/workflows/pages.yml` publishes `docs/` to the site. The verifier brief says to report that check as FAIL (waiting on merge and deploy) until the live page actually shows `--shout`. It must not pass it on the strength of the diff. The builder brief tells the builder to say this plainly in the PR description and not claim the line as met.

**Builder brief:** it opens with the four expect lines word for word; the issue has no non-goals. The steps are:
- Add `--shout` to `bin/greet.js`, before or after the name, so `--shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`.
- Leave plain output and the missing-name usage error (exit code 2) exactly as they are.
- Add tests to `test/greet.test.js`.
- Document the flag in `docs/index.md`.
- Run `npm test`, then open one PR.

**Verifier brief:** one check per expect line, in order:
1. **Upper case:** run `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js Ada --shout`. Both must exit 0 and print `HELLO, ADA!`.
2. **Output unchanged:** run the CLI without `--shout`, including with no arguments, at the PR head and at the base commit. Stdout, stderr and exit codes must match.
3. **Docs:** `docs/index.md` must contain `--shout` and say what it does.
4. **Published page:** confirm the PR is merged and the pages deploy has finished, then fetch the live page and look for `--shout`.

Test coverage and the `--shout` with no name case are listed under Advisory, outside the pass/fail conditions.
